items.name: Negative Feedback Example (Body Temperature)
items.description: body temperature rises above the set point (37°C) → thermoreceptors in the skin and brain detect the change → the hypothalamus (control center) signals the effectors → sweat glands release sweat and skin blood vessels dilate to release heat → temperature returns to the set point. When temperature drops, skin blood vessels constrict and shivering produces heat.

items.name: Hyper-
items.description: above, excessive, or more than normal (e.g., blood pressure or blood glucose that is higher than normal).

items.name: Hypo-
items.description: below, under, deficient, or less than normal (e.g., blood pressure or blood glucose that is lower than normal).

items.name: Brady-
items.description: slow (e.g., a heart rate below 60 beats per minute).

items.name: Tachy-
items.description: fast or rapid (e.g., a heart rate above 100 beats per minute).

items.name: Endo-
items.description: within, inside, or inner (e.g., the inner lining of the heart, or glands that secrete hormones directly into the blood).

items.name: Exo-
items.description: outside or outward (e.g., glands that release their secretions through ducts onto a surface, or a cell moving products out of the cell).

items.name: -itis
items.description: inflammation (e.g., inflammation of the appendix or of the tonsils).

items.name: -ectomy
items.description: surgical removal or excision (e.g., removal of the appendix or of the tonsils).

items.name: -ology
items.description: the study of (e.g., the study of cells or of tissues).

items.name: -emia
items.description: a condition of the blood (e.g., too few red blood cells, or too much potassium in the blood).

items.name: -cyte
items.description: cell (e.g., a red blood cell, a white blood cell, or a skin cell).

items.name: Circle of Willis
items.description: a ring of connected arteries at the base of the brain. Clinical significance: if one artery is blocked or narrowed, blood can be rerouted around the ring so the brain keeps its blood supply (collateral circulation); it is also a common site of brain (berry) aneurysms.

items.name: Support
items.description: bones form the framework of the body; they hold the body up, give it shape, and support soft tissues and organs.

items.name: Protection
items.description: bones shield internal organs from injury (e.g., the skull around the brain, the rib cage around the heart and lungs, the vertebrae around the spinal cord).

items.name: Movement
items.description: bones act as levers; skeletal muscles attached to bones by tendons pull on them to move the body (works with the muscular system).

items.name: Mineral Storage
items.description: bone stores calcium and phosphorus and releases them into the blood when needed to keep mineral levels balanced.

items.name: Blood Cell Production
items.description: red bone marrow inside bones makes red blood cells, white blood cells and platelets (hematopoiesis).

items.name: Diaphysis
items.description: the long, tube-shaped shaft of a long bone; made of thick compact bone surrounding the medullary cavity.

items.name: Epiphysis
items.description: the wider end of a long bone (proximal and distal); filled with spongy bone and covered with articular cartilage where it forms a joint.

items.name: Metaphysis
items.description: the region between the shaft and the end of a long bone; contains the epiphyseal (growth) plate in growing bones, which becomes the epiphyseal line in adults.

items.name: Periosteum
items.description: tough fibrous membrane covering the outer surface of bone (except at joint surfaces); contains blood vessels and nerves, anchors tendons and ligaments, and helps bone grow in width and heal.

items.name: Endosteum
items.description: thin membrane lining the inner surfaces of bone, including the medullary cavity; contains cells that build and break down bone during growth, repair and remodeling.

items.name: Medullary Cavity
items.description: the hollow space inside the shaft of a long bone; holds yellow bone marrow in adults (red marrow in children).

groups.name: Musculoskeletal System · Compact vs spongy bone, red vs yellow marrow

items.name: Compact Bone
items.description: dense, solid bone that forms the outer layer of all bones and the shaft of long bones; made of tightly packed osteons (Haversian systems); gives strength and support.

items.name: Spongy Bone
items.description: also called cancellous bone; lighter bone made of a lattice of thin plates (trabeculae) with spaces that hold red bone marrow; found in the ends of long bones and inside flat bones.

items.name: Red Marrow
items.description: blood-forming (hematopoietic) tissue that makes red blood cells, white blood cells and platelets; in adults found mainly in the spongy bone of flat bones (sternum, ribs, hip bones, vertebrae, skull) and the ends of long bones.

items.name: Yellow Marrow
items.description: mostly fat (adipose tissue) that stores energy; fills the medullary cavity of long bones in adults; can turn back into blood-forming marrow if the body needs more blood cells (e.g., after severe blood loss).
